items.prompt: How confident are you that you could list the separate pieces of a product and explain what deployment must answer for each one?
A deployed frontend calls http://localhost:8000/upload and the button does nothing for visitors. What does localhost refer to?

options.label: Whatever computer the code is running on — the visitor's own machine

items.explanation: Localhost always means this same computer, so a deployed frontend pointing at localhost looks for a backend on the visitor's own machine.

items.prompt: Take an app idea and list at least four of its pieces — for example frontend, backend, database, storage, AI, workers — and write where each one would run or what it would connect to.

criteria: Lists at least four distinct pieces of the system
Gives a plausible home or connection for each rather than treating the app as one thing

items.prompt: In your own words, explain the difference between code existing, code running, and a product operating.

criteria: Separates code stored in a repository from a process running somewhere
Explains that operating means all needed pieces serve users together

items.prompt: How confident are you that you could explain which parts of a system are disposable and which must survive?
The backend machine is replaced. What should happen to user accounts and uploaded videos?

options.label: They are recreated the next time each user logs in
They persist because they live in the database and object storage, not in the backend
They are lost unless users made their own backups

items.explanation: Compute is disposable and state must survive, so user data lives in persistent systems a new backend can reconnect to.

items.prompt: Take an app idea and sort five of its things into two lists: disposable (restartable compute, temporary files) and must-survive (accounts, uploads, records).

criteria: Sorts at least five items into the two lists
Correctly places user data and media in the must-survive list

items.prompt: In your own words, explain why storing uploads inside the backend machine is an architecture bug rather than a coding bug.

criteria: Explains that compute can be replaced while state must persist
Shows the consequence: a replacement backend starts with the files gone

items.prompt: How confident are you that you could decide whether a piece of work belongs in the request, a background job, or a media-delivery path?
An upload needs two minutes of video processing. What should the upload request do?

options.label: Hold the connection open until processing finishes
Store the upload, mark it processing, queue the job and respond immediately
Refuse the upload as too large

items.explanation: The request does the fast part and a worker does the slow part; the database tracks the status so the user can see it change.

items.prompt: List three tasks from an app idea and label each one: answer inside the request, do in the background, or deliver through a media/CDN path.

criteria: Each label matches the task's real wait time and size

items.prompt: In your own words, explain what a queue and a worker do for an application.

criteria: Describes the queue as a list of waiting work and the worker as the separate program that performs it
Explains the user gets an immediate response while status updates later

items.prompt: How confident are you that you could predict what a product should do when a dependency fails or usage multiplies by one hundred?
The AI provider goes down on a busy Friday night. What should the product do?

options.label: Take the whole site offline until it returns
Keep serving scores and video and mark summaries temporarily unavailable
Hide the failure so nobody notices

items.explanation: Graceful degradation keeps every feature that does not need the failed dependency working, with a clear temporary error for the rest.

items.prompt: Run the multiply-by-100 test on an app idea: name the first thing you think would break — backend capacity, database connections, AI rate limits, the processing queue or the cloud bill — and one fix for it.

criteria: Pairs it with a reasonable fix such as more capacity, caching, a queue or limits

items.prompt: In your own words, explain graceful degradation and give one example.

criteria: Explains that the product keeps working minus the failed part
Gives an example such as scores still working while AI summaries pause
